topic: Solid Material Changes by Bending, Pressing, Hammering, Cutting
key_concepts: Solid materials can be changed by bending, pressing, hammering, or cutting.
Bending can change a solid material's shape and size.
Pressing can change a solid material's size and shape.
Hammering can flatten or change the shape of a solid material.
Cutting changes a solid material's size and shape.
No new material is formed when solid materials are bent, pressed, hammered, or cut.
Only physical appearance or properties change in these processes.
Not all solid materials can be bent, pressed, hammered, or cut.
The ability to be bent, pressed, hammered, or cut depends on the material's properties.
Some materials are easily hammered, such as nails, tin cans, and steel bars.
Some materials are easily cut, such as cloth, hair, and paper.
Some materials are easily pressed, such as modeling clay and dough.
